The HEAT toolkit addresses stakeholder engagement by guiding users through the process of consulting and including diverse stakeholders in the design process, particularly focusing on marginalized and vulnerable groups. It emphasizes the importance of engaging stakeholders throughout the development and deployment stages to understand the potential harms and benefits of AI systems. Space 3 of the toolkit provides instructions on identifying relevant stakeholders and encourages meaningful and power-sensitive participation, while also addressing the risks of tokenism and participation-washing.

In terms of environmental sustainability, HEAT includes a section in Space 2 dedicated to assessing and mitigating the environmental impact of AI systems. This section introduces methods for calculating the carbon footprint of AI models and conducting Life Cycle Analysis. It also encourages users to rethink their product design with environmental considerations in mind, promoting more-than-human-centred design practices that acknowledge the interconnectedness of all living things. Thus, HEAT integrates both stakeholder engagement and environmental sustainability as critical components of responsible AI development.
